builtins.name: args.count
builtins.description: Number of command-line arguments, excluding the program name.
builtins.example: args.count() // e.g. 2, if the program was run with two arguments

builtins.name: args.get
builtins.description: The argument at `index`. Does not panic on an out-of-range index - it returns "" instead, the same way a missing environment variable does.
builtins.example: args.get(0) // the first CLI argument, or "" if none was passed

builtins.name: fs.exists
builtins.description: Whether a *file* exists at `path`. Confirmed live: this is file-only, not file-or-directory - it returns false for a path that is genuinely an existing directory (fixture.temp_dir's own result, for example). There is no builtin that checks directory existence.
builtins.example: fs.exists("config.json") // true if it exists as a file

builtins.name: fs.read_text
builtins.description: Reads a file's full contents as text.
builtins.failureMode: E0312 if the file can't be read.

builtins.name: fs.write_text
builtins.description: Writes `content` to `path`, creating or overwriting it; the bool reports whether the write succeeded, so a failed write is reported, not panicked on.

builtins.name: fs.try_read_text
builtins.description: Reads a file's full contents as text, returning Err instead of failing on a read error.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: fs.try_write_text
builtins.description: Writes `content` to `path`, returning Err instead of failing on a write error.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: fs.read_bytes
builtins.description: Reads a file's full contents as raw bytes.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: fs.write_bytes
builtins.description: Writes raw bytes to `path`, creating or overwriting it; the bool reports whether the write succeeded.

builtins.name: env.get
builtins.description: The environment variable's value, or "" if it isn't set - there is no way to tell "unset" apart from "set to the empty string" from this alone; use env.has first if that distinction matters.

builtins.name: env.has
builtins.description: Whether an environment variable is set, even to an empty value.
builtins.example: env.has("CI") // true inside most CI environments

builtins.name: env.set
builtins.description: Sets an environment variable for the current process (and anything it later spawns via process.run, unless overridden by process.run_with_env).

builtins.name: env.unset
builtins.description: Removes an environment variable from the current process.

builtins.name: process.run
builtins.description: Runs a process to completion and captures its exit code, stdout, and stderr. A failure to spawn the executable at all (e.g. it doesn't exist) is not distinguished from a timeout - both report exit code -1 through process.code.

builtins.name: process.run_with_input
builtins.description: Like process.run, piping `input` to the child process's stdin.
builtins.example: process.run_with_input("cat", [], "hi") // a process result with stdout "hi"

builtins.name: process.run_with_env
builtins.description: Like process.run, with `env` overriding environment variables for the child process only - the current process's own environment is restored once the call returns.
builtins.example: process.run_with_env("printenv", ["KEY"], map.set(map.new(), "KEY", "value")) // a process result with stdout "value"

builtins.name: process.run_with_options
builtins.description: Like process.run, with a working directory ("" for unchanged) and an optional timeout in milliseconds (<= 0 for none); a timed-out process is killed and reports exit code -1, the same code a failed-to-spawn process reports.

builtins.name: process.code
builtins.description: The child process's exit code (-1 for a timeout or a failed spawn).

builtins.name: process.stdout
builtins.description: The child process's captured standard output.

builtins.name: process.stderr
builtins.description: The child process's captured standard error.

builtins.name: process.ok
builtins.description: Whether the process exited with code 0.
builtins.example: process.ok(result) // true if exit code was 0

builtins.name: str.len
builtins.description: Number of bytes in a string (not necessarily the number of visible characters, for non-ASCII text).

builtins.name: str.trim
builtins.description: Removes leading and trailing whitespace.

builtins.name: str.upper
builtins.description: Converts to uppercase.

builtins.name: str.lower
builtins.description: Converts to lowercase.

builtins.name: str.from_int
builtins.description: Formats an int as decimal text.

builtins.name: str.to_int
builtins.description: Parses decimal text as an int; Err if it isn't a valid integer.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: str.contains
builtins.description: Whether `haystack` contains `needle`.

builtins.name: str.starts_with
builtins.description: Whether `value` starts with `prefix`.

builtins.name: str.ends_with
builtins.description: Whether `value` ends with `suffix`.

builtins.name: json.valid
builtins.description: Whether `text` parses as valid JSON of any shape (object, array, or scalar) - does not require it to be an object the way json.get does.

builtins.name: json.get
builtins.description: A top-level key's value from a JSON object, as text. There is no dotted/nested path support - only one flat, top-level key lookup.
builtins.failureMode: E0313 if `text` doesn't decode as a JSON object.

builtins.name: json.encode
builtins.description: Encodes a value (int/str/bool/list/record, recursively, plus enums including Option/Result) as a JSON string. Map is not supported and returns Err.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: path.join
builtins.description: Joins two path segments. Pure string concatenation with a separator - it does not special-case an absolute `b`, unlike some other languages' path-join.

builtins.name: path.basename
builtins.description: The final path component.

builtins.name: path.dirname
builtins.description: The path with its final component removed.

builtins.name: path.extension
builtins.description: The file extension, without the dot, or None if there isn't one.

builtins.name: path.stem
builtins.description: The final path component without its extension.

builtins.name: dir.list
builtins.description: Lists a directory's immediate entries. Names only (not full paths), unsorted, and not recursive - see dir.walk for that.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: dir.walk
builtins.description: Recursively lists files under `path` as full paths, files only (a subdirectory is recursed into, never included in the result itself). `maxDepth` 0 means only `path`'s own files; an unreadable subdirectory partway through the walk is silently skipped, not a failure.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: time.now
builtins.description: Current Unix epoch time in seconds.

builtins.name: time.to_iso
builtins.description: Formats epoch seconds as a UTC ISO-8601 string.

builtins.name: time.year
builtins.description: The UTC calendar year for epoch seconds.

builtins.name: time.month
builtins.description: The UTC calendar month (1-12) for epoch seconds.

builtins.name: time.day
builtins.description: The UTC calendar day of month for epoch seconds.

builtins.name: time.hour
builtins.description: The UTC hour (0-23) for epoch seconds.

builtins.name: time.minute
builtins.description: The UTC minute for epoch seconds.

builtins.name: time.second
builtins.description: The UTC second for epoch seconds.

builtins.name: time.format
builtins.description: Formats epoch seconds with a strftime-style pattern, evaluated in UTC.

builtins.name: time.in_timezone
builtins.description: An ISO-8601 string using `zone`'s own numeric UTC offset. `zone` is an IANA name like "America/New_York". Avoid relying on %Z/%z in a separate time.format call instead of this - those cannot reflect an arbitrary zone.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: time.format_in_timezone
builtins.description: Formats epoch seconds with a strftime-style pattern using `zone`'s zone- and DST-adjusted wall-clock time (year/month/day/hour/etc. are all zone-adjusted, unlike time.format's UTC-only fields).
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: duration.seconds
builtins.description: `n` seconds as a plain epoch-second count, for arithmetic like time.now() + duration.minutes(5).

builtins.name: duration.minutes
builtins.description: `n` minutes as a plain epoch-second count.

builtins.name: duration.hours
builtins.description: `n` hours as a plain epoch-second count.

builtins.name: duration.days
builtins.description: `n` days as a plain epoch-second count.

builtins.name: Duration.of_seconds
builtins.description: Builds a Duration of `n` seconds. Duration is a distinct record type, not a plain int, so it can't be mistaken for an unrelated int at compile time the way the duration.* plain-int helpers can be.

builtins.name: Duration.of_minutes
builtins.description: Builds a Duration of `n` minutes.

builtins.name: Duration.of_hours
builtins.description: Builds a Duration of `n` hours.

builtins.name: Duration.of_days
builtins.description: Builds a Duration of `n` days.

builtins.name: Duration.add
builtins.description: Sums two Durations.

builtins.name: Duration.sub
builtins.description: Subtracts one Duration from another.

builtins.name: Duration.scale
builtins.description: Multiplies a Duration by an integer factor.

builtins.name: Duration.to_seconds
builtins.description: A Duration's total length in seconds, for bridging back to plain epoch-second arithmetic. A Duration's own `seconds` field is also readable directly, since it's an ordinary record.

builtins.name: http.get
builtins.description: Sends an HTTP GET request. Windows only. The response body is bounded at a fixed 10 MiB limit; exceeding it is an Err, not a truncated body - see http.request_with_limit for a caller-chosen limit that truncates instead.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: http.post
builtins.description: Sends an HTTP POST request with a text body.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: http.put
builtins.description: Sends an HTTP PUT request with a text body.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: http.delete
builtins.description: Sends an HTTP DELETE request.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: http.request
builtins.description: Sends an HTTP request with a custom method and headers, for anything http.get/post/put/delete don't cover.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: http.request_with_limit
builtins.description: Like http.request, but a response over `maxBytes` returns Ok with a truncated body instead of an error - the one http.* call that doesn't error on hitting its size limit. `maxBytes` <= 0 means unlimited; see http.truncated to detect whether truncation happened.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.
builtins.example: http.request_with_limit("GET", url, headers, "", 1024) // Ok(response), possibly truncated

builtins.name: http.request_bytes
builtins.description: Like http.request, with a raw-bytes request body - for a body that isn't guaranteed valid text.
builtins.failureMode: Returns Err on failure; never panics.

builtins.name: http.status
builtins.description: An HTTP response's status code.

builtins.name: http.body
builtins.description: An HTTP response's body as text.

builtins.name: http.content_type
builtins.description: An HTTP response's Content-Type header value.

builtins.name: http.ok
builtins.description: Whether the response status indicates success (2xx).

builtins.name: http.body_bytes
builtins.description: An HTTP response's body as raw bytes, for a response that isn't guaranteed valid text.
builtins.example: http.body_bytes(response) // the response body as bytes

builtins.name: http.truncated
builtins.description: Whether the response body was cut short at a byte limit. Always false for a response from any call other than http.request_with_limit.
builtins.example: http.truncated(response) // false unless fetched via http.request_with_limit and cut short

builtins.name: list.len
builtins.description: Number of elements in a list.

builtins.name: list.get
builtins.description: The element at `index`. Bounds-check with list.len first when the index isn't already known-valid - there is no non-panicking variant.
builtins.failureMode: E0316 if `index` is out of bounds.

builtins.name: list.push
builtins.description: Returns a new list with `item` appended; `list` itself is unchanged, matching this language's immutable-by-default collection style.

builtins.name: list.map
builtins.description: Returns a new list with `callback` applied to every element. `callback` can be a named function reference (`&double`) or an immutable-capture closure.

builtins.name: list.filter
builtins.description: Returns a new list containing only the elements for which `callback` returns true, in their original order.

builtins.name: list.find
builtins.description: The first element for which `callback` returns true, or None if none matches.

builtins.name: list.fold
builtins.description: Reduces a list to a single value by applying `callback(accumulator, item)` left to right, starting from `initial`. An empty list returns `initial` unchanged.

builtins.name: map.new
builtins.description: An empty map. Its key/value types are pinned by the first real map.set/map.get used with it in the same expression - passing a bare map.new() into something requiring a concrete Map<K,V> before that happens can fail to type-check; chain a real map.set first, or see map.remove for building a genuinely empty typed map.

builtins.name: map.len
builtins.description: Number of entries in a map.

builtins.name: map.get
builtins.description: The value for `key`, or None if absent. Keys must be int, str, or bool (or a record/enum with an explicit `impl Eq`).

builtins.name: map.has
builtins.description: Whether `key` is present.

builtins.name: map.set
builtins.description: Returns a new map with `key` bound to `value`, inserted or overwritten; `map` itself is unchanged.
builtins.example: map.set(scores, "Ada", 92) // scores with Ada added or updated

builtins.name: map.remove
builtins.description: Returns a new map with `key` removed; a no-op (returns an equivalent map) if `key` was already absent.

builtins.name: map.keys
builtins.description: All keys, in unspecified order - don't rely on it matching insertion order.

builtins.name: map.values
builtins.description: All values, in unspecified order, aligned with map.keys' own order for the same map.

builtins.name: map.map
builtins.description: Returns a new map with `callback` applied to every value; keys pass through unchanged. `callback` takes the value only, never a (key, value) pair.

builtins.name: map.filter
builtins.description: Returns a new map containing only the entries whose value `callback` returns true for.

builtins.name: map.fold
builtins.description: Reduces a map's values to a single value by applying `callback(accumulator, value)`, starting from `initial` - same callback convention as list.fold, over values only.

builtins.name: result.ok
builtins.description: Wraps a value as a successful result, using this language's lowercase result<T,E> builtin convention (distinct from the capitalized Result enum - the two don't mix without result.to_result).

builtins.name: result.err
builtins.description: Wraps an error message as a failed result.

builtins.name: result.is_ok
builtins.description: Whether a result is Ok.

builtins.name: result.value
builtins.description: The success value. Check result.is_ok first (or handle both cases) rather than assuming Ok - there is no non-panicking variant.
builtins.failureMode: E0319 if the result is actually Err.

builtins.name: result.error
builtins.description: The error message. Check result.is_ok first (or handle both cases) rather than assuming Err.
builtins.failureMode: E0320 if the result is actually Ok.

builtins.name: result.to_result
builtins.description: Normalizes any result-shaped value - whichever of the two conventions produced it - to the same runtime representation, so existing callers typed against one don't need to change.
builtins.example: result.to_result(result.ok(5)) // Ok(5), same value either way

builtins.name: fixture.temp_dir
builtins.description: Creates and returns the path to a fresh, uniquely named temporary directory. No automatic cleanup - call fixture.cleanup when done.

builtins.name: fixture.cleanup
builtins.description: Recursively removes a directory, typically one created by fixture.temp_dir.

builtins.name: bytes.from_str
builtins.description: Converts text to bytes. bytes is represented identically to str at runtime (a deliberate scope reduction, not a NUL-safe binary type) - content with an embedded NUL byte truncates at the NUL on round-trip.

builtins.name: bytes.to_str
builtins.description: Converts bytes to text.

builtins.name: bytes.length
builtins.description: Number of bytes.

builtins.name: expect.equal
builtins.description: Asserts two values are equal; fails the current test (not the whole run) if not. Only usable inside a native `test "name" { ... }` block.

builtins.name: expect.true
builtins.description: Asserts a value is true; fails the current test if not.

builtins.name: expect.ok
builtins.description: Asserts a result is Ok; fails the current test if not.

builtins.name: expect.err
builtins.description: Asserts a result is Err; fails the current test if not.

builtins.name: expect.some
builtins.description: Asserts an Option is Some; fails the current test if not.

builtins.name: expect.exit_code
builtins.description: Asserts a process result's exit code equals `code`; fails the current test if not.

builtins.name: expect.stdout_contains
builtins.description: Asserts a process result's captured stdout contains `text`; fails the current test if not.

builtins.name: expect.stderr_contains
builtins.description: Asserts a process result's captured stderr contains `text`; fails the current test if not.
